  "text": "He laid it beside the first photograph. The gate had lost its paint in broad strips, but the car was the one she still drove.

“You said you'd never been.”

“I said I hadn't been inside.”

“What was he digging?”

She took the towel from the worktop and hung it over the oven handle. One end was longer. She straightened it.

“It wasn't for digging.”

He looked more closely. His father's hands rested on the spade's handle. The blade was clean, standing on the gravel.

“There was a dog,” she said. “He wouldn't get out without something to hold.”

“My father liked dogs.”

“Not this one.”

Outside, the boy called to someone. A second bin lid slammed.

He turned the photograph over. Nothing was written there, but a rectangle of paper had been peeled away, leaving a rough patch.

“Who took it?”

“The woman next door.”

“Does she still live there?”

“I don't know.”

He put the key in his pocket. She watched him do it.

“You can leave that here.”

“Why?”

“In case you lose it.”

He went to the window. Her car stood across the road with one wheel on the pavement. There was a new scrape along the passenger door, low down, where the paint had gathered into a white curl.

“When did you last go?”

She didn't answer.

He turned from the window. She had put the photographs together, one exactly covering the other.

“Did you pay them?”

“Only what I had with me,” she said."
